title: “I AM ONLY A CHILD.”
paragraphs: “I AM ONLY A CHILD.”
That was Jeremiah’s defense.

Not rebellion.
Not unbelief.
Just fear wearing humility’s mask.
God’s voice had just shattered the quiet.

“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you.
Before you were born I set you apart.” — Book of Jeremiah 1:5
Imagine hearing that.
Chosen before your first heartbeat.
Appointed before your first breath.
And Jeremiah’s response?
“I can’t.”

Not because God was unclear.
Not because the mission was vague.
But because the calling was bigger than his confidence.
Jeremiah looks at himself.

Young.
Inexperienced.
Unready.
“I am only a child.”
The Hebrew word na'ar can mean youth, servant, or inexperienced boy.
In other words:
“Lord… I’m not qualified.”
Sound familiar?
We say it differently.

I’m not ready.
Someone else can do it better.
I’m too broken.
Too unknown.
Too late.
But heaven answers Jeremiah with a thunderclap.

“Do not say, ‘I am only a youth.’
You must go to everyone I send you.” — Book of Jeremiah 1:7
Notice something powerful:
God did not argue about Jeremiah’s weakness.
He simply overruled it.
Then comes the moment that changes everything.
The Lord reaches out.
Touches Jeremiah’s mouth.
“I have put my words in your mouth.” — Book of Jeremiah 1:9
Jeremiah thought the problem was his age.
God knew the solution was His presence.
This is the pattern of God.

Moses stutters.
David is the forgotten shepherd.
Peter is impulsive and unstable.
Yet God calls them anyway.
Why?
Because God does not recruit the confident.
He creates the confident by His Spirit.
And centuries later, another young man would face a calling that looked impossible.

A carpenter’s son.
No throne.
No army.
Yet through Him, the world would be saved.
That man is Jesus Christ.
And through His cross, our greatest disqualification—sin—was answered by grace.
The Gospel tells us:
You were not called because you are ready.
You are called because Christ is enough.
So if your heart whispers tonight:

“I’m only a child.”
“I’m only a sinner.”
“I’m only a nobody.”
Listen carefully.
God’s answer has not changed.
“Do not say…”
Because when God calls,
He also touches the mouth, strengthens the heart, and sends the messenger.
🔥 Friend, what excuse have you been offering God?
Lay it down.

The same God who called Jeremiah
is still calling today.
And the invitation is the same:

Repent.
Trust Christ.
Follow the voice that knew you before you were born.

Because Jesus still turns
insecure people into Gospel carriers.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
